courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Field Trip in Geographical Science
courses.description: Field studies are an integral part of the study of geography and resource management. The benefits of field studies are enhanced by a study trip to a destination outside of Hong Kong. The objectives are three-fold: (1) to broaden students’ horizons and knowledge base through exposure to a different and less familiar environment outside Hong Kong; (2) to enable students to make comparative studies across different countries or regions; and (3) to provide an opportunity for students to interact with non-local scholars and students in the same discipline. This field trip course is held during term breaks under the supervision of one or more faculty members or invited trip leaders. The theme of the field trip can be relevant to the Concentration Area(s) under geography and resource management. Students are required to participate in all activities throughout the course and submit individual and/or group-based assignments.
courses.course_syllabus:
Part 1: Overview of field studies

* Overall briefing on non-local field studies (all the trips yearly) and registration

Part 2: Pre-trip preparations and orientation

* Introduction to the field trip destination and themes
* Briefing on the field trip requirements and logistics
* Pre-trip student presentations or other preparation work

Part 3: Field trip

* Visits and activities at the destination
* Visits and activities at the partner university(ies) or organisation(s)
* Fieldwork and learning activities related to the thematic Concentration Area(s) led by the trip leader(s)
* Data collection and research under the guidance of the trip leader(s)

Part 4: Post-trip reflection and assignments

* Post-trip student presentations and reflection on field trip experiences
* Submission of individual and/or group-based assignments
courses.required_readings: Required readings will be provided by respective trip leaders according to the theme and requirements of each trip.
courses.recommended_readings: Recommended readings will be provided by respective trip leaders according to the theme and requirements of each trip.

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Natural Resource Management
courses.description: Given that humankind worldwide depends on natural resources for survival, the course will provide an overview of the principles of natural resource management. The course will specifically be useful to students interested in understanding the issues associated with use and misuse of natural resources. Lectures, field trips, seminars and study assignments will be used to focus attention and help analyze natural resources according to biotic resources, physical and earth resources and the social sciences, by identifying principles and practices used to organize natural resources for human use. Understanding these principles will allow for environmentally sound management of natural resources. The understanding of the physical and earth resources will facilitate the prudent management of resources such as land, water, waste. Applying social sciences systems of inquiry will prepare students for understanding the management, administration and policy issues that could affect humanities use of natural resources, globally, regionally and locally.
courses.course_syllabus:
Lecture 1: Synopsis of Resource, Natural Resources and Natural Resource Management
Lecture 2: Evolution of Resources and Natural Resource Management
Lecture 3: Dealing with Ecosystem Management in Natural resource Management
Lecture 4: Methods of Evaluation in Natural resource Management: INRMP
Lecture 5: Sacred forests and Indigenous Management
Lecture 6: Wetland, Aquaculture and Fish Ecology: Guest Speaker.
Reading Week (Preparation of a conceptual framework for the INRMP)
Lecture 7: Conservation management and Adaptive management: A choice of convenience
Lecture 8: Class Forum (Presentation of the conceptual framework for the INRMP)
Lecture 9: Tangible use of natural resources: Food Security, food management and slow food
Lecture 10: Intangible use of natural resources: Protected Areas and parks management
Lecture 11: Community participation and perspectives on natural resource management
Lecture 12: Students presentation of the INRM projects

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Energy and Society
courses.description: The historical evolution of the human society is significantly affected by how we consume energy. Our modern society is built on modern energy consumption patterns. However, rising energy consumption also raises serious environmental challenges that are detrimental to human beings and our planet Earth. Accordingly, one critical goal of energy development is to maximize the positive impacts and to minimize the negative impacts of energy consumption. After discussing the role of energy consumption in a society, this course will analyze how energy consumption and the environment affect each other. Students will then be guided through various levels of a society, from individuals, households, communities, to cities, countries and the world in general discussion and case studies on how energy is consumed. Recognizing the importance of energy conservation as a key solution, this course will further examine two major barriers, particularly the behavior and efficiency gaps, to understand how we could achieve the goal. An open and especially active mind is a must for success in this course.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to be equipped with basic knowledge on energy consumption, from positive to negative impacts, from patterns to solutions. The course will train the students to approach problems with critical and creative thinking. Students will learn not only along the temporal dimension but also across various societies in the current world. Particular learning outcomes could be listed below:
 To understand major social, economic, political and environmental impacts of energy consumption
 To critically think about energy consumption in the real world from individual to global levels
 To examine how to achieve sustainable development from the perspective of energy consumption
 To learn basic analysis skills and design solutions on energy consumption and conservation
courses.course_syllabus:
The evolution of energy consumption
1. Historical evolution of energy consumption
2. Social impacts of energy consumption

The two-way linkage between energy consumption and the environment
3. Energy consumption and air pollution
4. Energy consumption and water
5. Energy consumption and climate change

Energy consumption and society
6. Energy consumption of an individual: activities, age, gender, income
7. Energy consumption of a household: sharing, housing, energy-related decision making
8. Energy consumption of a community: time spending, thermal comfort, weekly and seasonal cycles
9. Energy consumption of a city: commute, local climate
10. Energy consumption of a country: transportation network, industries, economic structure
11. Energy consumption of the world: energy and development

Energy conservation
12. The distance from lips to hands: the behavior gap
13. The distance from wallets to actions: the efficiency gap

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Field Studies in China
courses.description: Field studies is an integral part in the study of geography. The benefits of field studies are enhanced by a study trip to a destination outside of Hong Kong. The course is held during term breaks under the supervision of one or more faculty members. The destination of this trip is China. The trip will study urban and regional development, as well as resources and environmental issues in China. The objectives are three-fold: (1) to broaden students' horizon and knowledge base through exposure to a different and less familiar environment outside Hong Kong; (2) to enable students to make comparative studies across different countries or regions; and (3) to provide an opportunity for students to interact with overseas students and scholars in the same discipline. Students are required to participate in all activities throughout the trip and to submit an individual report afterwards.

The theme of the field trip can be one or more Concentration Area(s) under the programme curriculum. Students are required to participate in all activities throughout the course and submit individual and/or group-based assignments.
courses.course_syllabus:

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Satellite Image Analysis
courses.description:
This course discusses the application of digital image processing techniques in
analyzing digital remote sensing data. Topics include: image preprocessing, image enhancement, image classification and accuracy verification.
courses.learning_outcomes: This course discusses the concept and application of digital image processing techniques in analysing digital satellite data for geographical and environmental studies. Topics include: image preprocessing, image enhancement, image classification, accuracy verification and change detection. Upon completion of the course, students are expected to grasp basic understanding of the principle of digital remote sensing image analysis and how different processing techniques are applied in generating thematic information.

courses.description: This course covers major research and application issues in GIS. Topics include location allocation, route planning, spatial interpolation, 3D visualization, and web/wireless GIS. Through course project, lab sessions, and class discussions, it fosters an appreciation of GIS as an effective tool for solving complex geographical problems.
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of the course, it is expected that the students will be able to:

• Synthesize and integrate concepts of GIS theory and methodology, including data models, GIS architectures, and spatial analysis.
• Develop an understanding of advanced spatial analytical functionalities, including spatial interpolation, route planning, and location-allocation
• Gain an understanding of GIS platforms other than desktop GIS
• Demonstrate a working knowledge to solve transportation and other geographical issues using GIS

courses.title: Transport Geography
courses.description: Contemporary economic processes, such as the globalization of trade and the emergence of economic blocs, have been accompanied by significant growth in the movements of people and freight. This course provides a broad introduction to transport geography. Basic ideas in sustainable development will be related to the provision of infrastructure and services of transport and logistics at various geographical scales, and to the development of different modes of transport. The course will provide students with a foundation for more advanced treatments of the subject.

courses.title: Special Topics in Geography and Resource Management II
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth analysis of specific topics in geography, resource utilization and management that supplements other courses offered by the Department. The topics selected are of great significance to the sustainability of mankind. The content of the course will vary with the instructor. Important topics will include the theoretical background of the geographical and resource management issues concerned, geographical analysis using the latest geographical techniques, evaluation of resource availability and scarcity, optimal resource utilization and management.
courses.feedback_evaluation: Early Course Evaluation and Course Evaluation

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Environmental Planning and Assessment
courses.description: The course introduces and examines the theories, processes and methodologies of environmental planning and assessment as important tools and instruments for minimizing human impacts on the environment and achieving environmental sustainability through good governance. Environmental planning plays a vital role in urban design and the formulation of land use and other planning strategies in order to mitigate the effects of human activities on air, water, land, and ecological systems, and to promote sustainable use of energy, water and other natural resources. While the coverage is broad and comprehensive, emphasis will be placed on the two most prominent tools, i.e. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA), in terms of their origins, legal and regulatory requirements, and practices around the world. After introducing the conceptual framework and theoretical foundation of environmental assessment, specific methods and techniques (both qualitative and quantitative) will be introduced for students to understand the procedures and systems and gain the technical skills for practical applications. Environmental planning considerations and impact assessment will be examined for different sectors (industry, commercial, transportation, etc.) and multiple environmental media (air, water, solid waste, and noise) at difference spatial scales (local, regional, and national). Although a global perspective and comparative approach will be adopted throughout the course, examples and case studies of mitigating and managing environmental impacts through planning and assessment will mainly come from Hong Kong and mainland China.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To understand basic concepts and theories of environmental planning and assessment as important tools for minimizing environmental impacts and consequences of human activities,

2. To learn how legal, regulatory and institutional systems work together to influence and face the environmental planning challenges,

3. To gain technical skills and practical experiences of investigating environmental planning problems and assessing impacts, and

4. To develop holistic approaches to integrate social, political, and economic considerations into environmental planning and assessment processes.
courses.course_syllabus:
• Course Briefing and General introduction to environmental planning and assessment

• Elements, approaches and methodologies of environmental assessment

• Introduction to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), and its processes, tools and methods

• Tools, methods and techniques for impact prediction and assessment 1

• Tools, methods and techniques for impact prediction and assessment 2

• Environmental Impact Assessment at the international level

• Transboundary Environmental Impact Assessment

• Overview of Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA)

• Evaluating the SEA of Landuse Use Plans

• The practice of SEA in different countries

• Cost-Benefit Analysis and the valuation of environmental impacts

• Social Impact Assessment and Risk Assessment

• Cumulative Effects Assessment and Life-Cycle Assessment

courses.subject: GRMD

courses.description: This is an advanced course organized in seminar and workshop formats. Emerging geographical issues in Hong Kong related to land and water resources, transport and infrastructure development, housing and population policies, urban poverty, urban renewal, regional cooperation etc., will be selected for discussion and debate. The issues discussed will change from time to time in response to the changes in Hong Kong. Students are required to submit an issue-based investigation report at the end of the course.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected:

• to have thorough understanding on selected geographical issues

• to learn how to formulate problem, identify issues, undertake research and synthesize information

• to be capable of developing necessary skills for the analysis of geographical issues

• to obtain a basic proficiency in presentation and communication skills

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Environmental and Resource Economics and Policy
courses.description:
This course introduces the core tools of environmental and resource economics and applies them to real-world policy design. We begin with foundational microeconomics—demand and supply, price signals, and the role of incentives—then examine key concepts such as externalities, the tragedy of the commons, and the Environmental Kuznets Curve. Students learn how to value environmental goods and services, choose discount rates, and conduct cost-benefit analysis while weighing efficiency and equity.
The second half of the course focuses on policy instruments and market design. We compare incentive-based tools—emission taxes, compliance carbon markets, voluntary carbon markets, payments for ecosystem services, and waste charging schemes—evaluating when and why each works (or does not work) and implementation challenges. We connect to contemporary governance and disclosure frameworks via ESG, highlighting how firms, investors, and regulators translate environmental goals into action.
No prior coursework in economics is required. Regular attendance, timely review, and active participation are expected. Questions and constructive challenges are strongly encouraged. By the end of the semester, students will be able to analyze environmental problems with economic reasoning and assess which policy instruments are most effective, efficient, and equitable in different contexts.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After successfully completing this course, the students will be able to:

* Explain core concepts in environmental and resource economics and interpret their implications for policy.
* Apply environmental valuation methods, select appropriate discount rates, and conduct cost–benefit analysis that weighs efficiency and equity.
* Compare and evaluate incentive-based policy instruments—emission taxes, compliance and voluntary carbon markets, payments for ecosystem services, and waste charging—identifying when they work and key implementation challenges.
* Critically appraise empirical studies and ESG disclosures, analyze real-world case studies with economic reasoning, and communicate evidence-based policy recommendations clearly in writing and discussion
courses.course_syllabus:
1. ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance)
2. Demand & supply curve, price signal
3. Environmental Kuznets Curve
4. Externalities, tragedy of the commons

7. Cost-benefit analysis
8. Efficiency and equity
9. Emission tax

11. Voluntary carbon market
12. Payments for Ecosystem Services
13. Incentive-based pricing and waste charging

courses.subject: GRMD
courses.title: Urban Big Data Analysis and Application
courses.description: Urban areas, where nearly 70% of world’s population is projected to live and thrive in 2050, rely on loads of data to run smoothly every day. The concept of smart city brings together the innovative use and management of data and advancement of computational technology. The collected data are so massive and varied, coined as “Big Data”, that require novel techniques to store, process and analyse to support various applications in urban areas with a view to improve people’s lives in cities. This course is divided into two parts. The first part will introduce the fundamental concepts, methods and platforms to analyse urban big data. The second part will discuss the application of big data in various urban topics including urban planning, transportation, energy, extreme events and public health issues. Students will be equipped with knowledge and skills on big data analytics to deal with real-world challenges.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are able to:
• attain knowledge on the fundamental concepts and principles of big data, data mining and machine learning;
• acquire skills of the computing environment for big data and data analytics including hardware, software, distributed systems, and analytical tools; and
• understand the application of big data to various urban and geographical issues.
